processing: Fully oxidised orthodox black tea; the lot on record is a whole-leaf TGFOP1.
harvest_season: The second flush of May and June is the lot sold abroad under the garden's name, as is usual for prized Assam orthodox tea.
appearance_dry: Dark twisted leaf; as with other tippy Assam grades, the higher grades show golden buds.
appearance_liquor: Clear medium amber in the second flush lot on record.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown leaf, as usual for fully oxidised Assam orthodox tea.
taste_profile: A second flush lot was described as smooth, full-bodied and malty, with a nutty, biscuit-like finish, a hint of cocoa and little astringency.

brewing.notes: Normally brewed Western-style. It takes milk well if steeped on the long side, but try the first cup plain.

vintage_note: Sold by garden, grade and flush of the current year, with second flush (May and June) the lot most often exported. Like other Assam orthodox teas it is best drunk within a year or two. Availability is irregular: a lot appears at a retailer and then sells out.
description:
Panitola, also spelled Panitolla, is a garden in the Tinsukia district of upper Assam, known abroad through specialty tea merchants.

The lot on record is an orthodox second flush TGFOP1. Other grades may be sold under the garden's name, so check which one you are buying, because whole-leaf and broken teas brew very differently.

That TGFOP1 was described as full and malty, with nuts, biscuit, a little cocoa and a pear-like aroma, and with minimal astringency. Start with about three and a half minutes in near-boiling water and lengthen from there if you plan to add milk.

Look for the flush and grade on the label. Estate lots come and go, so treat a good one as a single purchase rather than a permanent shelf item.
history: Panitola is regarded in the trade as one of the older Assam gardens, and a tea merchant credits it with developing cultivars that lifted the quality of modern Assam orthodox tea. Those claims come from commercial descriptions. Its founding date and early owners are not well documented.
